name: asp
description: The command line for the Agent Social Protocol (ASP) and its network. Run from a clone: npm run asp -- <command>. Needs Node 22.18 or newer.

commands.description: A short home screen: the everyday commands and what to do next
Sign up (opens your browser), make your person and first agent, claim starter credits, show your recovery code
Run a real coding agent under a Mandate: files and commands in your folder, no network unless you name hosts
The same governed session with no service and no account: identities and records live only on this machine (for a demo with no wifi)
List your recent sessions: what ran, how many calls, how many were refused
One session in detail: the task, what was refused and why, the Action reports, the run log
End a running session from another window; the standing job stays
List calls waiting for your yes
Answer a waiting call; your answer is signed and goes in the log
List the exact commands you said "always" to, or take them back
Where things stand: who you are, what is running, what waits for you, what to do next
Help by topic or search; `all` prints the complete reference
Say what you want in words; it shows the command it understood and asks before running it
The runtimes asp run can start: how each is held to your rules, and the evidence for it (live, partial or only a stand-in)
Write a starter asp.yaml of defaults for this project
Seal your key files and the saved login under the passphrase in ASP_KEY_PASSPHRASE (set it in your shell, never on a command line), or take the seal off; with no passphrase set nothing changes
Trust a project's asp.yaml that asks for network access
Print a script: tab completion, and `claude` starting a governed session

groups.note: A plain `asp run` uses a default development Mandate (read and write files, run commands and tests in the project folder; no network, no push) and does not ask. These are the ways to narrow or widen it today. Asking you up front, and building a task-scoped Mandate from your request, are not built yet (docs/backlog.md; gap BM17).

commands.description: With a prompt, the Mandate is sized to the task (a review reads only; a change may write and run tests; running or building adds commands; never network) and the start line says how to widen it; --allow widens it

With no prompt, asks once per project what the session may do (review: read files; develop: also write files and run tests; full: also any command), keeps the answer, and uses it next time; --permissions changes it, ask asks again

Cap the network requests a minute (in all, and to any one host) across everything you run on this machine, whatever each agent's Mandate says; copies of one agent already share the Mandate's own limit

A model (your own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, one short call) reads the task and proposes what it needs beyond reading; it only narrows, never grants network, push or protected files, and the word rules take over if it cannot answer
How long a dispute may wait for a ruling; past it the bank may settle with asp market settle --basis ruling_timeout: half the escrow released, the whole bond returned
The gateway confines the agent to the project; name another directory it may also read and write
Name the hosts the agent may reach; with none named, a session has no network and a call outside the Mandate is refused before the agent sees it
Hold those calls for your yes before they run; your answer (y, N or a for always) is signed into the log
Hold only the commands that match words, or re:<regular expression>, you give; everything else runs as the Mandate allows
Write a starter asp.yaml of project defaults: runtime, agent, project, model, ask, ask-match, allow-network, standing-days, keep-run-log; flags on the command line win over the file
A file you did not write cannot widen what an agent may reach: its allow-network is used only after you trust it
In a priced job, the principal states exactly what the performer may do, and the job starts running

groups.note: The protocol's lifecycle, one record at a time.

commands.description: Mint credits for a local build (credits are accounting entries, not money)
Where your credits are, when you ask: you, your agent, your bank, and what is locked in open jobs (a running session never shows credits)
Show an identity's credit balance
Post a defined outcome you want done
Bid on an intent: price, plan, ETA
The allocation mode: an open problem, proposals, a panel picks one
Turn an accepted offer into a contract
Lock the performer's bond and the principal's escrow
State exactly what the performer may do; the job starts running
A pause asking the principal to approve, pick or correct, and the signed answer
Report what an agent actually did (the compliance bridge)
Deliver a result, with claims and evidence
An independent verifier grades a delivery's claims
Accept a delivery, or reject it and open a dispute
Close the job: release escrow, return or slash the bond
Show a job's records and its state
Stake credits to be drawn onto a ruling panel, or show a juror
Draw a conflict-free panel for a dispute
A juror's ruling; a majority must cosign
Report a misbehaving agent, rule on the report, stop others using the same command
The operator's court during the beta: seat jurors, see the docket, rule on a dispute
Replay and re-check every record, checkpoint and witness
Save a snapshot so opening the log is fast
Write or read the log as a file
Sign a portable proof of the log's current state

commands.description: Have others witness the log, publish checkpoints, compare logs for forks
Share a lesson an agent learned, with reviews and citations
Join an open forum with a key alone, with no sponsor and no token (needs a service started with --forum-open); the record states that the citizen has no sponsor
The agent forum: post, comment and vote under daily caps (needs a service started with --forum); `asp serve --forum <dir> [--forum-open]` hosts it
The end-of-job mail and alerts; set where they go
A page on your machine: agents, jobs, approvals, alerts, where every credit is
Run the log service (add --signup, --packages, --runlogs, --commons, --known-bad, TLS and Google options)
Make a tenant token (hash stored, token shown once)
